newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar falls below 112 yen in late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls below 112 yen in late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar broke below 112 yen in Tokyo on Tuesday, down more than three yen from its New York close on Monday, due to expections of a narrowing interest rate gap between the United States and Japan.
Selling of the dollar picked up speed with the start of trading in European centres, some of which had been closed on Monday for holidays.
The dollar fell as low as 111.98 yen, its lowest since December 6, 1996, on a wave of interbank and investor sales.
The dollar was also battered on Tuesday by worries that a sharp rise in Japan's trade surplus will spark friction with Washington.

Data released on Monday showed that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus grew 163.7 percent to 831.48 billion yen ($7.35 billion) in April and its trade gap with the United States soared 174.1 percent to 468.97 billion yen ($4.15 billion).

The market is avidly watching for the result of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later on Tuesday, but dealers said that even if U.S. rates are raised, this is unlikely to provide sustained support for the greenback. ($1=113 yen)
